evidence_note: Most limits are style-guide defaults, not trial results. Each 'why' points to a section of references/research.md. Angus's feedback overrides.

sentence_words.why: research.md section 2: sentence length has weak direct evidence. Soft 15 is a style default for working-memory load (section 1). Hard 25 matches Dyslexia Scotland.

clauses_per_sentence.why: research.md section 1: small phonological working memory; section 2: relative clauses are unsettled, so split anyway.

paragraph_lines.why: research.md section 3: paragraph spacing is the layout lever the AI holds; crowding evidence is moderate in children, weak in adults. Hard 5 matches Dyslexia Scotland.

paragraph_sentences.why: research.md section 3: one idea per short paragraph.

line_chars.why: research.md section 3: WCAG 1.4.8 says 80 characters or fewer. 60-70 is single-source guide direction.

long_word.why: research.md section 1: long, rare words cost the most (strong). Section 2: short and frequent words help (weak-moderate). Exact cut points are a judgement call.

passive_voice.why: research.md section 1: errors rise on passive and implausible sentences (weak-moderate). Active voice is a cheap default.

negation.why: research.md section 2: BDA says no double negatives. Study evidence is weak and not dyslexia-specific.

list_items.why: research.md section 1: many similar items add multi-item cost (weak). Short lists are a heuristic.

forbid.why: research.md section 3: italics read worse (moderate-weak). Underline and caps are guide advice (weak) but free to follow. Quiet pages: weak.

answer_position.why: research.md section 1: eye movement is laborious (moderate); fatigue evidence is thin (weak). Front-load so the reader can stop.

heading_after_lines.why: research.md section 3: real headings aid navigation (weak-moderate, BDA).

code_block_lines.why: research.md section 4: dyslexic programmers gaze at code differently (weak). Short blocks, one concern each.

code_line_chars.why: research.md section 3: 80-character guidance applies to unbroken code lines the client cannot wrap.

hash_chars.why: research.md section 4: hashes are hard to track (weak, background).

table_columns.why: research.md section 3: avoid wide tables that wrap badly (moderate).

abbreviation_first_use.why: research.md section 2: BDA says expand abbreviations on first use (weak-moderate).

look_alike_pairs.rule: warn when both words of a pair sit in one sentence
look_alike_pairs.why: research.md section 5: swap evidence is preliminary (weak). Cheap courtesy only.

word_swaps.why: research.md section 2: short common words help (weak-moderate). Rewrite the whole sentence; never patch single words (moderate).

bold_per_reply.why: research.md section 3: bold keeps letter shapes, italics read worse (moderate-weak). One bold phrase per reply. Whole-sentence bold dilutes the cue.

jargon.why: research.md section 2: BDA says explain jargon on first use (weak-moderate). Small list; the human pass finds the rest.

note_copy: This file is the one reread.mjs reads. The copy in ~/dev/dyslexic-reread is the research copy and can drift.
